title: What should you eat for a better night’s sleep?
reason: 上一课关注黄金、资产价值和金融风险，今天轮换到生产力与工作生活平衡。本集讨论饮食结构与睡眠质量的关系，同时提醒听众不要把社交媒体上的单一产品宣传当成简单答案，适合迁移到工程师值班恢复、个人精力管理和信息判断场景。练习先反复调用因果、对比和取舍表达，再逐步过渡到解释、改写和有限迁移，帮助把已经理解的高频表达转化为主动输出。

targetExpressions.expression: struggle to get a good night’s sleep
targetExpressions.meaning: find it difficult to sleep well at night
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to describe a sleep difficulty: I sometimes struggle to get a good night’s sleep after an on-call shift.

targetExpressions.meaning: know or recognise something from experience
targetExpressions.usage: Follow it with a noun or -ing form: Many people are familiar with lying awake even when they feel tired.

targetExpressions.meaning: have a connection or relationship with something
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when evidence shows a link without claiming direct cause: A healthier diet is associated with better-quality sleep.

targetExpressions.expression: be less about ... and more about ...
targetExpressions.meaning: emphasise that the second thing matters more than the first
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to correct the focus of a discussion: Better sleep is less about one food and more about the nutrients in your overall diet.

targetExpressions.meaning: give more attention to one option instead of another
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to show a deliberate priority: Experts suggest focusing on the whole diet rather than one supplement.

targetExpressions.meaning: there is no single simple solution that will fix a difficult problem
targetExpressions.usage: Use it before explaining why several factors matter: There is no magic bullet for better sleep.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Phil’s question: “Do you ever struggle ______ get a good night’s sleep?”
objectiveQuestions.targetExpression: struggle to get a good night’s sleep
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript uses “struggle to get a good night’s sleep”; struggle is followed by the to-infinitive.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Which sentence uses “be familiar with” naturally in the programme’s context?

options.text: Many people are familiar with the feeling of lying awake while tired.
Many people are familiar to the feeling of lying awake while tired.
Many people familiar the feeling of lying awake while tired.
Many people are familiar from the feeling of lying awake while tired.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript says many people are familiar with that feeling; the fixed preposition after familiar is with.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the research finding: a healthier diet is associated ______ better-quality sleep.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript reports an association between a healthier diet and better-quality sleep, using “associated with”.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What does “a healthier diet is associated with better-quality sleep” safely communicate?

options.text: Studies found a relationship between the two.
Every healthy meal immediately causes deep sleep.
Diet is the only factor that affects sleep.
The researchers did not study diet at all.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: “Associated with” expresses a link found in studies; the programme does not claim an immediate or exclusive cause.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the contrast: good sleep is less about one particular food and more ______ particular nutrients.
objectiveQuestions.targetExpression: be less about ... and more about ...
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript contrasts particular foods with particular nutrients using “less about ... and more about ...”.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Which advice best matches the experts’ main point?

options.text: Focus on the whole diet rather than one fruit or supplement.
Focus only on a magical powder advertised online.
Avoid fibre because it is linked with less deep sleep.
Replace every meal with one supplement.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The programme says focusing on the whole diet, rather than one fruit or supplement, is likely to be most effective.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the recommendation: focus on the overall eating pattern rather ______ a quick fix.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: “Rather than” introduces the option that receives less attention, here a quick fix.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: When the sleep doctor says “there is no magic bullet”, what does she mean?

options.text: No single simple product can solve the sleep problem immediately.
A specific supplement has been proven to work for everyone.
Social media does not contain any information about sleep.
Diet has no relationship with sleep quality.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The doctor rejects claims that one powder or tablet can improve sleep immediately; a magic bullet is a simple effective solution that usually does not exist.

assessment.retellingPrompt: Without looking at the full transcript, retell the episode in 80–120 words using this structure: (1) topic—the link between diet and sleep; (2) two key findings—what eating pattern is associated with more deep sleep and why the whole diet matters; (3) conclusion—why one supplement is not a simple solution. Phrase bank: “be associated with”, “focus on ... rather than ...”, “there is no magic bullet”. Use at least two phrases naturally. Simple, accurate sentences are enough; uncommon vocabulary and complex sentence structures are not required.
referencePoints: Long-term studies found that a healthier diet is associated with better-quality sleep.
Mediterranean-style diets contain more fruit, vegetables and whole grains, and less sugar and animal-based food.
Diets higher in fibre and lower in saturated fats are associated with more deep sleep.
Research on specific foods such as kiwi fruit and tart cherry juice is limited.
Experts recommend focusing on the whole diet rather than one fruit or supplement.
The sleep doctor says there is no magic bullet that will improve sleep immediately.
